text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Electoral commission suspends run-off local council election due on Thursday in federal capital Abuja pending investigations into rival claims by the political parties.
- Premises of some failed banks which were unable to meet a March 31 deadline to recapitalise have been sealed up in various parts of the country, Daily Times survey shows.
- State oil firm NNPC is considering Vienna, Geneva or Paris to site its European coordinating office following closure of its London bureau last month.
- Fuel output at Nigerian refineries are running at only 43 percent of national demand, accounting for current petrol scarcity in some parts of the country.
- Lagos state military administrator Colonel Mohammed Marwa enacts much-awaited rent edict, setting out how much rent is payable throughout the state and establishing tribunals to enforce it.
- Negotiations for new salaries for civil servants suspended pending the release of the national minimum wage, says secretary of the negotiating council, Sylvester Ejiofor.
- The five reinsurance firms in Nigeria need 333 million naira to meet new capital base set for them by the government.

- Hearing in bail application by dissidents charged with treason over Lagos bomb blasts adjourned to next Monday following confusion as to whether the complainant in the case is Lagos state or federal government.
- Banks freeze deposit rates despite getting higher returns from treasury bills.
- Four locomotives arrive from China which is handling a project to revitalise Nigerian railways; more expected soon.
- Nigerian-British chamber of commerce blames low inflow of foreign investment into Nigeria on poor infrastructure.
- Shares of Golden Guinea brewery enliven stock market as they are heavily traded on Wednesday at the stock exchange.
